title: Alleged victim speaks out after former Coffee Co. deputy accused of tracking her is released on bond

reading.body:
This is an insider misuse case, not a model error. A person with legitimate access to law enforcement systems is accused of querying them for a purpose they were never provisioned for. The Flock camera system, the tag reader system and the Georgia Crime Information Center database are built to serve police work, and the alleged use here was personal tracking of a woman without her consent. The failure sits at the point of access, where an authorised user's queries are executed because the system cannot tell an official lookup from a private one.

Catching this kind of misuse requires auditing who searched for whom and why, and treating a pattern of queries about one person as a signal rather than routine traffic. The reporting does not say what logging or review was in place, or whether any alert fired before the investigation began. It also does not say how the conduct came to light.

The charges are allegations. An indictment is not a conviction, and the account of the woman involved is her account. Whether Rozar is guilty of any count is not established by the reporting summarised here.

reports.title: Alleged victim speaks out after former Coffee Co. deputy accused of tracking her is released on bond

summary:
A former Coffee County sheriff’s deputy, Chris Ashley Rozar, 49, was released on bond on May 5 after a grand jury indicted him on eight counts. The charges include four counts of violation of oath by a public officer, two counts of computer invasion of privacy, one count of prohibited use of captured license plate data, and one count of stalking. Investigators say he misused the sheriff’s office Flock camera system, tag reader system, and the Georgia Crime Information Center database for personal reasons, including tracking a woman without her consent. He was fired when the investigation began.

The woman involved spoke anonymously, saying she waited two years for the investigation and hopes her story helps other women report abuse. The Georgia Bureau of Investigation led the case after former Sheriff Doyle Wooten requested it in 2024. Rozar was arrested on May 5 and released on bond the same day. He is scheduled for arraignment on May 27 in Coffee County Superior Court.
